defects.description: The splitter floors every share and discards the remainder, so the output parts do not add up to the input total.
defects.why_missed: The suite only splits totals divisible by the part count, so floor division produces an exact sum on every tested input.

defects.description: Errors thrown by split() inside run() are written to stdout instead of stderr.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'import { run } from "./src/split.js"; let stdout = ""; let stderr = ""; const status = run(["1", "101"], { out: { write: (text) => { stdout += text; } }, err: { write: (text) => { stderr += text; } } }); console.log(JSON.stringify({ status, stdout, stderr }));'

defects.why_missed: The suite only exercises successful split calls, so it never checks which stream receives an error raised inside run().

traps.description: A request for more than 100 parts is intentionally rejected with a usage error rather than silently capped.
